hook: Aidan Gomez studied mathematics and computer science as an undergraduate at the University of Toronto, working with Roger Grosse, before interning as a student researcher at Google Brain. There, working alongside Jakob Uszkoreit and other Google Brain researchers, he was one of eight co-authors of the 2017 paper Attention Is All You Need, which introduced the Transformer architecture that replaced recurrence and convolution with self-attention and went on to underpin most later large language models. He also co-authored the Reversible Residual Network (RevNet) paper on memory-efficient deep network training. He then pursued doctoral studies in machine learning at the University of Oxford, advised by Yarin Gal and Yee Whye Teh, while leading a research team at the nonprofit lab FOR.ai. In 2019 he co-founded Cohere in Toronto, where as CEO he has helped the company raise close to a billion dollars across four funding rounds and build enterprise-focused large language models.
name: Aidan Gomez

quote.text: I would conjecture that it is our ability to recognize patterns that spurred the development of our complex communication tool, language.
quote.context: From Aidan Gomez's blog post On Creating Artificial Intelligence, blog.aidangomez.ca, December 13, 2015

primary.name: Attention Is All You Need, arXiv:1706.03762
